title: 36.5 A Low-Latency 200Gb/s PAM-4 Heterogeneous Transceiver in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS and 28nm CMOS for Retimed Pluggable Optics
problem: AI infrastructure demands 200G/lane serial links for data-center interconnects, but linear-drive pluggable optics (LPO) face severe challenges at 200G: very-short-reach (VSR) channel insertion loss increases by 14dB at 2x data rate (to -14dB overall), and retimed LPO solutions (with DSP) introduce unacceptable latency (incompatible with low-latency AI inference requirements). Traditional 200G retimed schemes mitigate 30dB insertion loss via DSP compensation, but this adds significant pipeline delay.
motivation: AI inference workloads prioritize ultra-low latency; standard 200G retimed solutions with DSP compensation conflict with latency budgets, creating a need for non-ADC-based, low-latency architectures.
method: The transceiver transmits 200G per lane using two semiconductor technologies on the same chip: an older 0.13µm SiGe (silicon-germanium) analog front-end that conditions the signal directly in analog form, and modern 28nm CMOS digital logic for clock recovery and network functions. Instead of converting the weak incoming signal to digital and cleaning it up with DSP (digital signal processing, which adds processing delay), the analog side directly filters out the -14dB insertion loss from the fiber channel. This non-ADC receiver approach keeps latency near zero while achieving competitive energy efficiency.
key_novelty: A non-ADC receiver design combining 0.13µm SiGe and 28nm CMOS that eliminates DSP delay for 200G/lane transmission by filtering signals directly in analog form, enabling low-latency AI networks.
contributions: Non-ADC-based 200Gb/s PAM-4 receiver eliminating DSP latency overhead
Heterogeneous SiGe BiCMOS + CMOS integration enabling analog equalization without digital compensation
Mitigates VSR channel insertion loss (-14dB) via analog domain processing
Energy efficiency comparable to retimed solutions with significantly lower latency
primary_theme: Low-latency 200Gb/s heterogeneous transceiver for AI data-center links
